reading: The Australian Museum is a Sydney natural history, science and cultural institution that collects, researches, conserves and shares knowledge of Australia and the Pacific. Its site moves between fossils and living biodiversity, reef fieldwork, climate solutions, exhibitions, education and citizen science. It treats collections as sources of ongoing research rather than mere displays, and also foregrounds First Nations and Pasifika living cultures, community access and repatriation. Its vocabulary includes specimens, collection areas, taxonomy, fieldwork, conservation, Country, species identification, citizen science and discovery. Distinctive juxtapositions include a gigantic Patagotitan alongside tiny reef cleaners, frog calls contributed from backyards alongside museum research, and two centuries of accumulated material alongside current science and community-led work. The visitor experience also makes room for audio description, Auslan and quieter sensory-friendly visits.

enemies.idea: Type Specimen: a many-jointed cataloguer pins a label to anything it meets, then tries to make every other creature conform to that specimen's measurements.
enemies.why: Its classification creates a visible rule the crew can exploit by swapping labels or presenting a contradictory specimen.

enemies.idea: Distribution Mapper: a globe of collection records redraws the range of each organism it detects, then sends little survey drones to move the organism inside its newly assigned boundary.
enemies.why: An enemy that attacks by changing where you are allowed to be turns a map into a tactical puzzle.

enemies.idea: Freezer Custodian: a frozen-tissue carrier flash-freezes traces shed by the crew and grows brittle duplicates from them, each melting rapidly away from its cold source.
enemies.why: The crew can use heat and distance against copies made from their own trail.

enemies.idea: Reef Doctor: a cleaner-wrasse machine offers a helpful inspection, then strips useful fittings from equipment it mistakes for parasites.
enemies.why: Letting it close may repair damage or cost a prized tool; decoy fittings can distract it.

enemies.idea: Patagotitan Gantry: a colossal modular skeleton reaches through several galleries at once, placing each foot only where its tiny attendant surveyors have measured enough floor.
enemies.why: Its scale is felt across rooms, while its careful surveyors give the crew a way to redirect its steps.

enemies.idea: Minmi Armourer: a low, plated machine gathers fallen debris onto its back, becoming harder to damage but slower and more prone to jamming in narrow passages.
enemies.why: The fight changes as its scavenged armour accumulates, inviting the crew to lure it into a bottleneck.

enemies.idea: Afrovenator and Jobaria: a paired predator and giant whose automated pursuit routine keeps repeating; each lap knocks loose more material for the swarm to harvest.
enemies.why: The crew can interrupt the loop or steer the chase into other enemies.

enemies.idea: Frog-call Counterfeiters: hopping recorders answer a real croak with a convincing mechanical chorus, attracting surveyors to places where there are no frogs.
enemies.why: Listening for a chorus that repeats too perfectly lets a careful crew distinguish a trap from a living signal.

enemies.idea: Fossil Dater: a rolling instrument assigns an age to everything it scans and coats the 'oldest' target in a fast-hardening sediment shell.
enemies.why: A deliberately aged decoy can draw its preserving spray away from a trapped ally.

enemies.idea: DigiVol Transcriber: a little swarm reads handwritten specimen records and stamps its mistaken interpretations onto physical objects, forcing them into the wrong storage crates.
enemies.why: Ambiguous handwriting becomes a playful means of redirecting the swarm's logistics.

enemies.idea: Coral Spawning Collector: once its timer strikes, a cloud of drones releases buoyant metal beads that stick together around lights and moving equipment.
enemies.why: The predictable synchronized release lets the crew prepare currents, screens or a tempting light.

enemies.idea: Sediment Sifter: a reef research machine vacuums the floor to measure productivity, burying anything behind it under sorted dunes of grit.
enemies.why: Its wake creates both cover and a growing obstacle, so position matters more than brute force.

enemies.idea: Insect Hotel Foreman: an oversized bundle of drilled tubes recruits tiny machines into different chambers, each chamber producing a specialist for a different material.
enemies.why: Blocking or swapping tubes changes which threats emerge and makes the nest a practical target.

enemies.idea: pH Tester: a paper-strip skimmer samples every puddle and changes its own tools according to the colour it reads, mistaking harmless coloured liquids for dangerous chemistry.
enemies.why: The crew can trick its response with colour and turn an experiment into a diversion.

enemies.idea: Web Identifier: a spider-shaped sensor spins several distinct mechanical web patterns, then hunts whatever disturbs the pattern it has selected for study.
enemies.why: Each web telegraphs a different detection zone that observant players can learn to cross.

enemies.idea: Heatwave Forecaster: a floating reef model projects hot zones ahead of the crew; its own heaters then make the predicted zones come true.
enemies.why: The forecast is both a warning and the attack, giving the crew a chance to break the feedback loop.

enemies.idea: Pipefish Brooder: a long, narrow machine carries a row of detachable egg-like repair pods along its trunk; damaged pods hatch into tiny mechanics.
enemies.why: Targeting the carrier carelessly produces more opponents, while separating the pods offers another solution.

enemies.idea: Genome Weaver: an eight-legged assembler splices together strands of recovered machine instructions, producing mismatched limbs that adapt to whatever dismantled its last creation.
enemies.why: Repeated tactics change the next encounter, while interrupting assembly leaves a useful weakness.

enemies.idea: Treasured Finds Appraiser: a rolling examination bench identifies every unfamiliar object as a rare find and tries to carry it away for closer study, including the crew's tools.
enemies.why: A convincing oddity makes excellent bait, and retrieving confiscated gear creates a compact heist.

enemies.idea: Renovator: a net-zero design machine keeps retrofitting rooms with salvaged panels and insulation, sealing passages as it optimizes a building no one can now enter.
enemies.why: The crew can reuse its materials and anticipate its next modification to open a route.

enemies.idea: Touring Tyrannosaur: a transport crate unfolds into a mechanical skeleton whose separate sections keep trying to reunite at the next exhibition venue.
enemies.why: A chase can be broken into manageable moving parts, each with a destination the crew can manipulate.

enemies.idea: Nature Photographer: a lens-bodied machine freezes anything caught in its beam into a rigid tableau while it adjusts for the perfect wildlife image.
enemies.why: Shadows and reflections become cover, and the pose gives companions a brief chance to intervene.

allies.idea: FrogID listeners: a resilient network of backyard recorders compares natural calls and warns crews when the counterfeit chorus starts repeating.
allies.why: A distributed listening network supplies clues without needing a single vulnerable headquarters.

allies.idea: The quiet-hours keeper maintains a low-light, low-noise refuge and can guide a crew through it at a pace they choose.
allies.why: A genuinely calmer space changes the rhythm of a dangerous expedition and offers an alternate route.

allies.idea: Collection conservators assemble protective packing and safe handling plans for threatened specimens; they ask crews to retrieve materials rather than fight every machine.
allies.why: Their practical requests turn salvage into a rescue mission with fragile cargo.

allies.idea: Reef station field team tracks spawning and currents, lending crews a tide-timed route through the collector drones.
allies.why: Local observation gives the crew a useful window that feels earned by the site's research setting.

allies.idea: Community-led return team identifies the proper custodians for sensitive collection material and arranges its safe passage away from the swarm.
allies.why: The crew can help with transport and protection while the community retains authority over the material.

bosses.idea: The Total Collection: a vast mobile archive of specimen drawers, reef instruments and fossil scaffolds, determined to preserve all life by cataloguing it into immobility. Each defeated arm reorganizes the battlefield into a different collection area.
bosses.why: It brings the museum's breadth together in phases, with the central contradiction that preservation has become confinement.

bosses.idea: The Third-Century Curator: an anniversary machine stitching two hundred years of museum memories, fossils and future plans into a single endlessly expanding procession. It recruits every object it passes for one final, never-ending celebration.
bosses.why: A moving procession lets crews dismantle its gathering mechanism piece by piece instead of merely attacking a giant body.

bosses.idea: The False Atlas: a continent-sized projection fed by corrupted frog calls, specimen ranges and research records; its survey machines reshape the building to match its faulty model of biodiversity.
bosses.why: Restoring trustworthy observations changes the arena and gives the crew a concrete way to challenge the boss's authority.

events.idea: A real frog calls from behind a wall while mechanical imitators repeat the same recording nearby. Locate the irregular live call before the survey drones seal the wrong room.
events.why: A small listening mystery gives the crew a chance to rescue a living animal.

events.idea: A travelling dinosaur crate has come apart in transit; its tail is blocking a passage while the rest of the skeleton patiently waits for it around a corner.
events.why: The crew can negotiate the moving pieces, reassemble them or find a way around.

events.idea: During the coral spawning timer, beads drift toward a trapped research buoy. Alter the current or move a light to draw the beads away before they set.
events.why: A time-limited environmental puzzle uses the swarm's predictable behaviour.

events.idea: A visitor's treasured stone has been taken for examination by an appraiser machine. Offer it a stranger-looking scrap long enough to recover the stone.
events.why: The solution rewards curiosity about what the machine considers interesting.

events.idea: A quiet morning refuge is about to be disturbed by a noisy repair swarm. Reroute the machines while the people inside choose when and how to leave.
events.why: The crew protects a useful calm space through timing and care.

events.idea: A field team needs an uncorrupted sample from a cleaner station, but a reef-doctor machine keeps removing the sample container as 'debris'.
events.why: A disguise or decoy solves a problem created by misplaced helpfulness.

events.idea: A conservation crew has three fragile specimens to pack and only enough padding for two. Find more packing or choose a slower, safer route before the next tremor.
events.why: The constraint makes protection and logistics as engaging as combat.

events.idea: A map-making machine has assigned a corridor to an animal that cannot fit through it. Its delivery drones are now trying to force the issue.
events.why: The crew can fix the record, redirect the delivery or physically open a larger route.

events.idea: A homemade insect hotel is filling with machine larvae instead of insects. Remove its occupied tubes in the right order before the inhabitants scatter.
events.why: An ordinary hands-on activity becomes a delicate disarming challenge.

events.idea: A forecasting projector predicts heat in a gallery full of vulnerable supplies. Its heaters are warming up to make the prediction accurate.
events.why: The crew can save the supplies or break the cause of the forecast, with time for both if they split up.

events.idea: A pair of partial dinosaur skeletons has been sorted into the wrong transport frames; their locomotion routines keep pulling the frames in opposite directions.
events.why: Matching the parts correctly turns a chaotic obstruction into a usable distraction.

events.idea: An audio-description guide still works, but its next stop lies behind a swarm of lens machines. Follow its spatial descriptions through a dark route where the lenses cannot see.
events.why: Listening becomes a practical navigation tool and opens a distinct route through the encounter.

events.idea: A team preparing a community-led return needs a clear route and suitable packing for protected cargo. The crew can hold the route and gather supplies under the team's direction.
events.why: The mission gives the crew a concrete protective role while keeping decisions with the community.

events.idea: A renovation machine has insulated a room so thoroughly that a field team's equipment is trapped inside. Its next cycle will reuse any panel removed from the wall.
events.why: The crew can exploit the machine's reuse routine to build an exit instead of demolishing the room.

events.idea: A photograph machine waits for a perfect image of a mechanical reef tableau. Cross its field of view using moving shadows while it constantly reframes.
events.why: Its search for composition creates a readable, shifting stealth challenge.
